answer: Attestation-graph trust resists sybils by pricing identity on history. Like a river seen through a prism, one account breaks into visible traces: who it traded with, what it paid, when it acted. New identities start at near zero and must wander through real transactions to earn trust. A fake army can mint addresses for free but cannot fake months of costly interactions, so its influence stays capped while established agents keep full weight. Reputation costs time and fees that cannot be transferred.
